source_evidence: Hedge funds typically limit opportunities to redeem, or cash in, your shares to four times a year or fewer. They also often impose a lock-up period of one year or more, during which you cannot cash in your shares.
question: How do redemption limits and lock-up periods affect when a hedge fund investor can cash in their shares?
answer: Redemption limits restrict how often investors can cash in their shares; hedge funds typically allow this four times a year or fewer. A lock-up period is a separate restriction: during that period, often one year or more, investors cannot cash in their shares.
